title: Immunoinformatics Approach to Design a Chimeric CD70-Peptide Vaccine against Renal Cell Carcinoma
source: Science TLDR podcast episode show notes
one_line: A fully in silico immunoinformatics pipeline was used to design multiepitope chimeric vaccine constructs from CD70 epitopes fused to a cell-penetrating peptide and full-length TNF-α as adjuvant for renal cell carcinoma.
key_claims: Multiple immunogenic CD70 epitopes (CD70 is overexpressed in RCC) were predicted and filtered for antigenicity, non-allergenicity and non-toxicity.
Final constructs combined CD70 CD8+ and CD4+ T cell epitopes with a cell-penetrating peptide and the complete TNF-α sequence as adjuvant.
Docking predicted strong binding affinity of the constructs to the TNF receptor, argued to support uptake by antigen-presenting cells.
Molecular dynamics simulations indicated the vaccine–receptor complex is stable; in silico cloning with codon optimisation predicted high expression in E. coli.
Immune simulation predicted B cell activation, T cell proliferation and IFN-γ and IL-2 production.
limitations: Entirely computational: no in vitro or in vivo validation of immunogenicity was performed (authors call for this).
No safety or efficacy assessment in preclinical or clinical settings.
Delivery method not optimised and potential side effects uninvestigated.
Binding, stability and immune responses are predictions from modelling tools, not measured data.
Show notes report no quantitative affinity, stability or expression values.
open_questions: Does the construct, when expressed and administered, elicit CD70-specific CD8+ and CD4+ T cell responses in animal models?
Does predicted TNF-receptor binding translate to real antigen-presenting cell uptake and activation?
Is targeting CD70 tolerable given its expression on normal activated immune cells?
